Requested service: Total shoulder replacement  
CPT: 23472  
Reference number: POC-47F0C5AA4B-91233  
Date of denial notice: August 7, 2026  

Dear Humana Grievances and Appeals:

I appeal Humana’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 23472, total shoulder replacement. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

Please reconsider the request using the complete clinical information summarized below. The records document progressive, function-limiting shoulder disease, failure of extensive conservative treatment, objective structural joint destruction, and the absence of documented contraindications.

Clinical documentation supporting medical necessity:

1. Progressive symptoms and functional impairment

I have experienced nine months of progressive shoulder pain that has not been relieved by rest. The condition substantially limits daily activities. I cannot reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side.

On examination, there is glenohumeral crepitus. Active forward elevation is limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation is limited to 10 degrees. These findings demonstrate substantial loss of shoulder motion and function.

2. Failure of conservative treatment

The prior authorization packet includes a physical therapy discharge note documenting 24 completed supervised visits from March 16, 2026, through June 22, 2026. Treatment focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening over 14 weeks.

I also used NSAIDs for four months without adequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on May 13, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief. The persistent symptoms despite physical therapy, medication, and injection support the need for operative treatment.

3. Objective imaging findings

Shoulder radiographs obtained on June 21, 2026, using true AP and axillary views, show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. CT imaging confirms an intact rotator cuff.

These imaging findings establish advanced structural disease of the glenohumeral joint and support the requested total shoulder replacement.

4. Relevant examination and risk information

Cuff strength is intact. There is no active infection or untreated substance use. BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker. These records do not identify a documented contraindication to the requested procedure.

The requested procedure is recommended by Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery, based on the documented symptoms, functional limitations, examination findings, failed conservative care, and imaging results.

The plan’s specific medical policy or clinical-review guideline was not included in the denial notice, and I was unable to retrieve and verify the policy text publicly. Accordingly, I am not quoting or attributing any medical-necessity language to Humana in this appeal. Please identify the exact Humana policy or clinical-review criteria, including the version and effective date, that were applied to CPT 23472 in this case. If Humana believes additional information is required, please specify each missing item and allow the treating surgeon an opportunity to provide it.

Please reverse the denial and authorize CPT 23472. If Humana continues to deny the request, please provide a detailed written explanation identifying the specific clinical requirement that was not met, the records considered, the records found incomplete, and the policy or clinical-review criteria applied.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Avery Hayes  
Member ID: W379220601
